name: a reflex

VINIT.justification: the pre-stimulus baseline state before signal detection

TANCH.justification: the closure of the arc returning the muscle to a set point

AFWD.justification: the unidirectional propagation of an action potential toward the spinal cord

AREV.justification: the descending regulation that dampens the motor response

CLINK.justification: the chemical coupling of sensory input to motor output

IMSCRIB.justification: the muscle spindle recognizing its own length transformation

FSPLIT.justification: signal branches into an excitatory motor path and an inhibitory interneuron path

FFUSE.justification: reconstitution of the somatic command from opposing neural signals

EVALT.justification: the stimulus reaches the requisite voltage for propagation

EVALF.justification: failure to reach threshold or active suppression of the signal

ENGAGR.justification: the simultaneous contraction and stretch held in the musculoskeletal system

IFIX.justification: the neuroplastic record of the reflex event in the spinal logic

phase_3.void_description: polarized resting potential without signal flux
phase_3.true_description: excitatory postsynaptic potential above firing threshold
phase_3.false_description: inhibitory postsynaptic potential below firing threshold
phase_3.both_description: co-contraction of limb muscle groups maintaining isometric posture

steps.domain_action: muscle spindle exists in a state of high electrical potential energy
spindle monitors its current geometric state to establish identity
mechanical stretch triggers a localized gated sodium influx
action potential travels down the afferent nerve fiber
the sensory event is logged by peripheral nerve adaptation
the signal enters the spinal cord and splits into primary and secondary arcs
the primary branch drives the excitatory alpha motor neuron
the excitatory signal bifurcates for local contraction and cortical reporting
signal propagates toward the neuromuscular junction
local and central motor intent reconcile at the ventral horn
the secondary branch activates an inhibitory interneuron to relax the antagonist
inhibitory signal descends to prevent conflicting kinetic energy
the total limb state reconciles through agonist-antagonist coordination
the motor neuron releases acetylcholine into the synaptic cleft
the motor discharge occurs as an irreversible physical contraction
the muscle enters a momentary state of both tension and length correction
muscle fibers shorten in direct proportion to the initial stretch stimulus
the muscle returns toward the original resting length
the spindle recognizes the return to the baseline identity
the system resets to the original homeostatic boundary

phase_5.ipc_mechanism: neurotransmitter diffusion across the synaptic cleft
phase_5.alfs_store: genetic encoding of the somatic nervous system architecture

phase_6.pre_cycle_state: high ionic gradient across the axonal membrane
phase_6.post_cycle_state: restored ionic gradient via sodium-potassium pumps
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — metabolic energy consumption restores the electrical potential to the initial low-entropy state
